name: the-locks-go
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-before-real-data.md: A1 to A8, B1 to B6, C1 to C3, D, R1 to R11 and "finding N" are its own numbers. Sid's decisions are in src-store/README.md, "Decisions of 12 October 2026 — before real data is kept", and win over the contract; "entry N" is entry N of that section. "The build's page" is PROGRESS.md in src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/before-real-data/, and "ruling N" is point N of its "Rulings": each is the build session's, and where a ruling and another paper differ, the ruling holds. "The implied spec" is IMPLICIT_SPEC.md in the same folder: its sections by number, J1 to J22 of 3.3, the rows of 4.9, the points of 5.1 and of 5.3, the edges of 5.2, the operations 6.1 to 6.9, the matrix 7.1 to 7.6, P1 to P22 and section 9. Ruling N answers PN, and ruling 20 answers P20 to P22. "The stream probe" is stream-probe/RESULTS.md in that folder, and "the batch probe" is reads/batch-probe/RESULTS.md beside it: each is a probe, and no form, name or table comes from one. "The store's page" is src-store/softland/store/README.md, and "the proofs' map" is test-store/softland/store/README.md. src-store/CLAUDE.md binds every file. The rig, the server and Inland are examples: nothing comes from their code.

WHY THIS IS ONE PART, AND WHAT IT TOOK IN. Its one hard part is to take the locks and the seal out of a store that stands, so that no job of theirs goes unseen (A5, held against the whole list of implied spec 3.3, J1 to J22) and no check is left passing for a wrong reason (A8; finding 16; implied spec 5.1, its last paragraph). It is not cut smaller, because no half of it can be stated as a tree that is whole: the door, the declaration, both gates, the door's reads and five of the six proofs hold the seal together (implied spec 3.1, 3.2, and 5.1, "What today's proofs assert that part A makes untrue"). It took in C1 to C3. C plans no state. It changes the act's form and the declaration, whose rules and words this part changes anyway, and checks of the same proofs (implied spec 5.3, its last paragraph). And C2's bound is, like A6's, a bound that a gate holds on an act that the door no longer stops (rulings 3 and 17; implied spec P17, what the bound "stands beside"). A cycle of its own for C would write those checks a second time.

HOW THE STAGE DOC IS READ. This part designs no new state. Its operations are the calls and the steps of today's store that it changes. Its state is what the store keeps no more, and the one form that it chooses.

OPERATIONS OWNED.
(1) A1 to A8, whole, as rulings 1 to 6 and 19 read them: a send through the door, a gate's decision of an act whose values are plain, and the door's other calls (implied spec 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3; 5.1, points 1 to 16, and the paragraph "What goes away with the request for locks, beside the locks").
(2) C1 to C3, whole, as rulings 16 and 17 read them, with the last line of the contract's part C ("Not here"): an act under a deep permission, and a give (implied spec 5.3, points 1 to 8; 6.7).
(3) R4. Of R9, the heads that this part makes untrue: in BUILD-store-module.md, item 7 of "What to build", rules 5, 15 and 16, and of rule 20 what R9 names; in BUILD-door.md, all that R9 names. Ruling 7 says how.
(4) Of the matrix: 7.1, its first five blocks, for the reads A, P, L and S; 7.2 and 7.4; but in each of them the block "x a rebuild".
(5) Of section 9: of "From 'When this build passes'", items 1, 2, 5 and 6; of "What the contract asks elsewhere", its last line, which is the run of ruling 19 and the first of the "Three things of the paper that are no open point" on the build's page.
(6) Of the contract's "The builder chooses": its first line and its last. Of "Not decided": its second line, kept as ruling 20 says and built as R10 asks.
(7) For the receipt: the list of A5; how deep a permission can be (C3); and each thing that rulings 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 20 say Sid hears.

WHAT TO FIGURE OUT.
1. Where each job of the locks and of the seal goes, J1 to J22 and any that the plan finds beyond them, before anything is taken out (A5).
2. What the store keeps no more, and what each thing that read or wrote it does in its place: A3; A1's last sentence as ruling 2 reads it; implied spec 4.4, 5.1 points 15 and 16, and J17 to J22.
3. The form in which a thing is on a log of acts and under the door's digest, now that nothing is sealed (ruling 19, with its one condition; implied spec 5.1, points 5, 6 and 9; J13 and J14). The parts after it stand on this form: the digest of B1 is of it, and the rows of B3 are made from it. So it is left such that B1, B3 and ruling 14 can be met. This part builds nothing of B.
4. What a gate says of each thing that the door no longer stops: A2; A4, with ruling 1 for what the door still drops; A6 as ruling 3 reads it; rulings 4 and 5; implied spec 5.1, points 8, 10, 11 and 13.
5. The bounds on a permission and on an act once C1's number is gone: where the one depth is held and that the two roads agree on it (ruling 16; C3; implied spec 5.3, points 1 to 5); and what C2's bound counts, with its number and its word (ruling 17; finding 14; implied spec 5.3, points 6 and 7; P17).
6. Each word that it makes, and each word of the locks and of the seal that leaves (R8; ruling 4 for the thing that gets no word).

THE TREE AS THIS PART LEAVES IT. The six proofs pass, each changed where this part makes one of its lines untrue and nowhere else (A8; implied spec 5.1 and 5.3, the two paragraphs on what today's proofs assert). The run that is no check (the proofs' map, "The measures") still runs. Each explanation that this part makes untrue is replaced, as the contract's "Explanations, as the tree's rules say" asks: of the lines that it names, the first two; and the words of the locks and of the seal leave the lists.

NOT THIS PART'S. A log of answers, a rebuild, a measure of D. Nothing under the contract's "Not in this build, by decision".
needs_from_the_parts_before: Nothing of this build. It stands on the store as it is when its plan starts, and on the six count lines of the build's page, "The starting point, confirmed". Its plan does not wait for the stream probe.

The store's page, by its heads; the plan finds every line. The rows of "The parts" for the door, for door/ and for module/; "How the parts relate"; "What the gate does not check, said plainly", where it speaks of the stop at the request (finding 1); under "Engineering choices": "The value in a fact's row is plain, and a String", "How locks are asked for and read", "The cipher", "Closing" for the reason that goes (implied spec J19), "One copy of a lock's bytes", the two paragraphs "What one accepted act costs ..."; and of "How each of the builder's rules is met" the numbers 5, 15, 16, 20 and 21, and in 19 what it says of a lock.
The folder maps and the namespace docstrings of each file that implied spec 3.1 lists. The two files that go take their rows of door/README.md with them.
The proofs' map: the section of each proof whose checks go or change. test-store/README.md where it names a lock.
risks_the_plan_settles_first: Ruling 19's one condition, by a run before the form is fixed (implied spec 5.1, point 9; J13; finding 7 as the implied spec checked it, "What it rests on").
That the list of A5 is whole before anything is taken out.
Where a gate counts a plain value before it reads a row, for a refused act too, and how often the text of a value is made (ruling 3; implied spec 5.1, point 11; 6.2, "How soon").
That the two roads of a permission agree on one depth, and what a deep permission costs before any check refuses it (ruling 16; implied spec 5.3, points 1 to 5).
What C2's bound counts, against what a deep permission costs once it stands (ruling 17; implied spec 5.3, point 6; P17).
The checks of the door's proof that rest on a time, once no send meets a request (the proofs' map, "The checks that rest on a time").
What the read path's proof and the measures hold of a request, or of a seal made by a proof's own hand (implied spec 5.1, "The read path's proof").
the_split_in_short:
Three parts, in this order: the-locks-go (A1 to A8, C1 to C3), answers-in-a-log (B1, B2, B6, half of B5, D, and the runs before the plan), the-rebuild (B3, B4, the other half of B5, R1). Each has one hard part. It is not the contract's own reading into A, B, C and D, for three reasons. B holds two hard parts that share no mechanism: a change inside each gate, which is hard in what a failed attempt leaves, and a reading of the logs, which is hard in each part of each row. The stage doc asks that such parts be separate, and says that state which only a later part reads belongs to the part that writes it. C plans no state, and changes the same forms and the same checks as A. D plans no thing of the store.

The cuts that were weighed and not made. (1) A in two, the door before the gates, or the values before the tables of locks. Neither half can be stated as a tree that is whole: a store whose door seals nothing and whose gates refuse a value that is not sealed passes no proof. (2) C as a part of its own, after A: see notes, 4. (3) answers-in-a-log cut by gate. Whether there is one log or one for each gate is the plan's to choose (the contract's "The builder chooses", its second line), and a cut by gate would choose it in this paper. (4) The comparison apart from the rebuild: a proof belongs with what it proves. (5) D as a part of its own: its code is test code, and its numbers are of two trees; see notes, 3.

coverage_of_the_contract.how_to_read: Each thing is owned by one part. Where one line of the contract holds two things that can be told apart, each is owned once, and the row says which words are whose. A rule that the work of more than one part could break is owned by the last such part, which is the stage doc's rule for what cuts across; each part before it keeps the rule for what it changes.
coverage_of_the_contract.B3: the-rebuild. Two of its sentences name a thing that a log holds or comes to hold: a stray, as ruling 8 reads it, and the last stamp of a batch, as ruling 15 reads it. Putting each into a log is answers-in-a-log's.
coverage_of_the_contract.B5: By its two halves. "what the log of answers holds after a failed attempt of each gate", "with a run": answers-in-a-log. "how the rebuild comes to the answer that the tables hold": the-rebuild, on what answers-in-a-log left in the logs for it (ruling 11).
coverage_of_the_contract.C, its last line (\"Not here\"): the-locks-go. No part changes what a gate reads of a permission.
coverage_of_the_contract.D: answers-in-a-log: the three measures, and the code that measures. The first number, and what the second stands beside, are of the tree as the-locks-go leaves it. Who runs them, and when, is in notes, 3.
coverage_of_the_contract.Runs before the plan is fixed, 1 to 3: answers-in-a-log. The stream probe is making them; that part's plan reads them, and makes more where its own questions need them.
coverage_of_the_contract.R2: the-rebuild, as the last part that touches a log. Kept by the-locks-go through A7, and by answers-in-a-log through B6 and ruling 15.
coverage_of_the_contract.R3: the-rebuild, as the last part: it is the one reader, and it shows that no other is there. Kept by answers-in-a-log through B2 and ruling 11.
coverage_of_the_contract.R4: the-locks-go. No later part touches anything that comes before the log.
coverage_of_the_contract.R5: the-rebuild, as the last part: it is the one part that makes tables of its own. Kept by answers-in-a-log for when a reader can learn of a decision.
coverage_of_the_contract.R6: the-rebuild, as the last part, by ruling 18. Each part keeps it for its new code; implied spec section 2 is the list that it is held against.
coverage_of_the_contract.R7: By the two halves of ruling 12. "of the tables", and the first of its two properties: answers-in-a-log. "of what a rebuild makes from the logs", and the second: the-rebuild. the-locks-go keeps it for the checks of a second attempt that it changes (implied spec J19).
coverage_of_the_contract.R8: the-rebuild, as the last part, for the lists as a whole. Each part lists the words that it makes; the-locks-go takes the words of the locks and of the seal off the lists.
coverage_of_the_contract.R9:
By its heads. the-locks-go: in BUILD-store-module.md item 7, rules 5, 15 and 16, and of rule 20 what R9 names; in BUILD-door.md all that R9 names. the-rebuild: rules 9 and
19. Ruling 7 says how. answers-in-a-log replaces, on the store's page, the sentences under those rules that it makes untrue.
coverage_of_the_contract.R10: By its two things, each where its kept answer is code. The depth of a permission: the-locks-go. The order of acts after a failure: answers-in-a-log, with D's third measure.
coverage_of_the_contract.R11: the-rebuild, as the last part; ruling 9's first point is its known case. Each part keeps it for each default that it chooses, and lists the choice as provisional.
coverage_of_the_contract.Not decided — kept only so that the buil: Its first line: answers-in-a-log. Its second line: the-locks-go.
coverage_of_the_contract.The builder chooses, and lists as provis: Its first and fifth lines: the-locks-go. Its second and third: answers-in-a-log. Its fourth: the-rebuild.
coverage_of_the_contract.Explanations, as the tree's rules say: Each part, for what it makes untrue. Of the five lines that the section names: the first two, the-locks-go; the third and the fifth, answers-in-a-log; the fourth, the-rebuild. The words that leave the lists: the-locks-go. The page for the rebuild, and the row of the proofs' README: the-rebuild.
coverage_of_the_contract.The receipt's lists: The jobs of the locks and of the seal, and how deep a permission can be: the-locks-go. The measures: answers-in-a-log. Every table with what it is made again from, and each thing that is not made again: the-rebuild.

coverage_of_section_9.From \"When this build passes\", 6: the-locks-go, for the lines of 5.1 and 5.3 that it names. Each part ends with every proof passing.
coverage_of_section_9.What the contract asks elsewhere, line 1: answers-in-a-log, for what the log of answers holds after it. That the rebuild then comes to the tables' answer is ruling 12's second property, in the-rebuild.
coverage_of_section_9.What a pass does not show: the-rebuild, in the map of the rebuild's proof. Its last sentence, the receipt's first line, is the build session's.

rulings_by_part.the-locks-go: 1 to 6, 16, 17 and 19. Of 7, its own lines. Of 20, the depth of a permission, and the facts beside entry 7.
rulings_by_part.answers-in-a-log: 11, 15, and 12 for the choice, for its first property and for the showing of both by a plan. Of 8, the entry. Of 9, its third and fourth points. Of 18, its last sentence. Of 7, its own lines. Of 20, the order of acts after a failure.
rulings_by_part.the-rebuild: 10, 13, 14 and 18. 9 but its third and fourth points. Of 8, the sets. Of 12, its second property, by a run. Of 7, its own lines.

checklist_of_the_stage_doc: Every hard part has its own part, and no trivial part is left unfolded: the taking out of the locks, with C folded in; the keeping of an answer, with D and the runs folded in; the rebuild, with its proof.

Nothing duplicated: each scope points by number, by head or by a short quoted phrase. A search of the three scopes for digits finds only pointers: the numbers of items, rulings, rules, sections, points, edges, rows, lines and findings, the marks of a scope's own lists, and the date in a section's name. No number, bound or limit of the contract is in a scope.

Every operation is owned once, and together the scopes cover the contract: the fields coverage_of_the_contract and coverage_of_section_9. Two lines, B5 and R7, are owned by halves; ruling 12 tells the halves apart.
State that a later part reads is in the scope of the part that writes it, with a pointer to what binds it: in the-locks-go, item 3; in answers-in-a-log, items 1 to 5.

No design: no depot, table, row, topology, name or mechanism is chosen by this paper. Where a scope names a thing of today's code, it is today's, and it is named because the contract or a ruling names it. The fields beside "scope" name heads of pages, and each guess is marked.

No boundary was rejected for looking hard. The two that were rejected, A in two and the cut by gate, were rejected because a scope could not be stated: the first leaves no tree that is whole, and the second chooses in this paper what the contract gives to the plan.

Failures found while the paper was checked, and their fixes. (a) B5 and R7 were first given whole to one part; each holds two things, and they are now owned by halves. (b) D's first measure was first given to the-locks-go and its code to two parts; D is now whole in answers-in-a-log, with its first number said to be of the tree before that part changes the module. (c) A scope said where in a gate's run an answer is kept; that is one of the two orders of implied spec P12, which the plan chooses, and the words went. (d) A scope counted the jobs of the locks; the count is now the pointer J1 to J22.
The stage doc asks for a reasoning log. This stage was allowed one file, so this field is the log.
notes:
FOR THE WHOLE BUILD, to rule before any plan starts.

1. Where rulings and the split pull against each other: "the plan" is two plans. Rulings 8, 9 (its third and fourth points), 11, 12 and 15 each give a choice to "the plan". Each of those choices is of what a log holds, so this paper gives each to the plan of answers-in-a-log, and the-rebuild takes them as made. What that costs: ruling 12's second property, ruling 8's sets made from entries, and B3's "every part of a row" are shown by a run only when the-rebuild is built. Until then they rest on a plan, reasoned. If the-rebuild finds a part of a row that the logs cannot give, answers-in-a-log is opened again. A guard that the build session can rule on: the plan of the-rebuild is written and checked before the build of answers-in-a-log is called passed.

2. Rulings 14 and 15. Ruling 14 asks that the rebuild's proof hand the rebuild an answer that no gate of today would give. Ruling 15 says that the log which holds a batch's last stamp takes no client's append. If that log is the log of answers, a proof cannot append such an answer to it. The scope of answers-in-a-log, item 5, points at ruling 14 so that its plan leaves this within reach; nothing is chosen here.

3. D. The build's page has "the measures of the contract's section D" as a stage after the review. Two of D's numbers are of a tree that is gone by then: the first, and what the second stands beside, are of the tree as the-locks-go leaves it. Either the build of answers-in-a-log takes them before it changes the module, as its scope says, or the stage runs the measuring code on the commit of the-locks-go. This paper says which part owns the code and of which tree each number is; who runs them is the build session's to rule.

4. C inside the-locks-go. If the build session wants C apart, it lifts out as a part between the-locks-go and answers-in-a-log, and no other scope changes. It takes with it: operations (2); of (5), item 5 of section 9; of (6), the last line of "The builder chooses" and the second line of "Not decided"; of (7), how deep a permission can be; item 5 of "What to figure out"; and ruling 16, ruling 17 and the depth in ruling 20. What that would cost: the checks of the act's form and of the declaration are written by A and then again by C, and C2's bound is planned after A6's and not beside it.

5. The runs before the plan. Only the plan of answers-in-a-log waits for the stream probe. The plan of the-locks-go can start now.

6. One paragraph of the store's page is made untrue three times: number 19 of "How each of the builder's rules is met". the-locks-go makes untrue what it says of a lock, answers-in-a-log what it says a rebuild would not give again, the-rebuild its first sentence. Each part replaces what it makes untrue, so the paragraph is written three times. That is what leaving the tree whole after each part costs.

7. What could be given to no part. Nothing of "What to build", of R1 to R11, of the runs before the plan, or of section 9. What stays with the build session and is no part's: the starting point, the commits, the receipt with its first line and with the citation that implied spec 1.3 names in its point 10, and the review of the whole.

scope:

"The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-before-real-data.md: A1 to A8, B1 to B6, C1 to C3, D, R1 to R11 and "finding N" are its own numbers. Sid's decisions are in src-store/README.md, "Decisions of 12 October 2026 — before real data is kept", and win over the contract; "entry N" is entry N of that section. "The build's page" is PROGRESS.md in src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/before-real-data/, and "ruling N" is point N of its "Rulings": each is the build session's, and where a ruling and another paper differ, the ruling holds. "The implied spec" is IMPLICIT_SPEC.md in the same folder: its sections by number, J1 to J22 of 3.3, the rows of 4.9, the points of 5.1 and of 5.3, the edges of 5.2, the operations 6.1 to 6.9, the matrix 7.1 to 7.6, P1 to P22 and section 9. WHY THIS IS A PART OF ITS OWN, AND WHAT IT TOOK IN. Its one hard part is that a gate keeps what it decided in a log as well as in its tables, and that what an attempt which did not count leaves in that log does no harm (B1, B5, R7 as ruling 12 reads it; implied spec 5.2, edges 2 to 5, and 6.4). It is apart from the rebuild for two reasons. The two share no mechanism: this is a change inside each gate, and what is hard in it is what Rama keeps and what it drops when an event or an attempt of a batch fails (the stream probe; the batch probe; implied spec 5.2, "What Rama gives"); the rebuild is a reading of logs, and what is hard in it is each part of each row (implied spec, section 4). And by the stage doc the logs are this part's deliverable: state that only a later part reads belongs to the part that writes it. It is not cut by gate: whether there is one log or one for each gate, and what an entry holds, is one choice for both gates and is the plan's (the contract's "The builder chooses", its second line), and a cut by gate would make that choice in the split. It took in D whole. D plans no thing of the store; its second and third numbers are of what this part changes; and its first is the number that the second stands beside.

HOW THE STAGE DOC IS READ. This part changes both gates of a module that is built. Its one operation is the keeping of an answer. Its state is what the logs hold, which only the part after reads.

OPERATIONS OWNED.
(1) B1, B2 and B6, whole: the keeping of an answer in a log (implied spec 6.4; 5.2, "What must hold of the log of answers itself" and "Which decisions get an entry").
(2) Of B5, its first half: what the log of answers holds after a failed attempt of each gate, "with a run". Of R7, the half that ruling 12 calls "of the tables", and the first of ruling 12's two properties.
(3) Of B3, the two things of which it says that a log holds them or comes to hold them: a stray, as ruling 8 reads it, and the last stamp of a batch, as ruling 15 reads it (findings 8 and 10).
(4) The contract's "Runs before the plan is fixed", 1 to 3: read from the stream probe when it is done, with more runs where this part's plan needs them (the build's page, the paragraph that starts "Where the build session placed the contract's runs").
(5) D, whole: its three measures, and the code that measures. Its first number, and what its second stands beside, are of the tree as the part before left it, so they are taken before this part changes the module. Finding 15 binds each. Of "Not decided", the first line, kept as ruling 20 says and built as R10 asks.
(6) Of the matrix: the read N in 7.1 and 7.5, and 7.1's block of an attempt that did not count. Where 7.1 says that N holds nothing of a stray, ruling 8 holds.
(7) Of section 9: of "From 'When this build passes'", item 3; of "What the contract asks elsewhere", its first line; and "The measures of D".
(8) Of the contract's "The builder chooses": its second line, and its third, because how an entry that counted is told from one that did not is a choice of what the logs hold (ruling 11).
(9) Of R9, no head. On the store's page it replaces each sentence that it makes untrue (ruling 7).

WHAT TO FIGURE OUT. Each is state that this part writes and that only the part after reads. Each is bound, by reference, by the requirements named. This part builds no rebuild and no comparison.
1. The log, or the logs, that hold what each gate decided: what an entry holds (B1), for which things (implied spec 5.2, "Which decisions get an entry"), how it is kept (B6; ruling 15), where it is declared (ruling 18, its last sentence), who reads it (B2; ruling 11), and when a reader can learn of a decision (R5). Finding 16, its first sentence, binds any table that this part adds or changes.
2. What tells an entry that counted from one of an attempt that did not, for each gate (ruling 11; implied spec 5.2, edges 2 to 5), such that both properties of ruling 12 hold at every point of failure that a run found real. This part's plan shows both. The second is shown by a run only when the rebuild is built.
3. What a log holds of a batch of the base that no act and no answer holds: ruling 15; implied spec 4.9, rows 4 and 5. And of ruling 9, the two choices that turn on what a log holds: the kept clock of a batch (its third point; implied spec 4.7; edge 25) and `:turns` (its fourth point; implied spec 4.6; 4.9, row 8). They are made here, because this part writes the logs; the part after takes them as made.

name: the-rebuild
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-before-real-data.md: A1 to A8, B1 to B6, C1 to C3, D, R1 to R11 and "finding N" are its own numbers. Sid's decisions are in src-store/README.md, "Decisions of 12 October 2026 — before real data is kept", and win over the contract; "entry N" is entry N of that section. "The build's page" is PROGRESS.md in src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/before-real-data/, and "ruling N" is point N of its "Rulings": each is the build session's, and where a ruling and another paper differ, the ruling holds. "The implied spec" is IMPLICIT_SPEC.md in the same folder: its sections by number, J1 to J22 of 3.3, the rows of 4.9, the points of 5.1 and of 5.3, the edges of 5.2, the operations 6.1 to 6.9, the matrix 7.1 to 7.6, P1 to P22 and section 9. Ruling N answers PN, and ruling 20 answers P20 to P22. "The stream probe" is stream-probe/RESULTS.md in that folder, and "the batch probe" is reads/batch-probe/RESULTS.md beside it: each is a probe, and no form, name or table comes from one. "The store's page" is src-store/softland/store/README.md, and "the proofs' map" is test-store/softland/store/README.md. src-store/CLAUDE.md binds every file. The rig, the server and Inland are examples: nothing comes from their code.

WHY THIS IS A PART OF ITS OWN. Its one hard part is to make every table that a gate writes, and every part of each row, again from the logs alone, by applying the answers that the log holds and deciding nothing (B3, R1; implied spec section 4 and 5.2), and to prove it by setting what it made beside what the gates wrote (B4). It is the last part because it reads only what the two parts before it leave: acts whose values are plain, and the logs. Its proof is in it and is no part of its own: a proof belongs with what it proves, and the comparison is the one test of what the contract calls "reasoned, not designed and not run" ("What this page rests on", its last line).

HOW THE STAGE DOC IS READ. This part adds code of the store that no act and no read passes through. Its operations are the rebuild and the comparison. Its state is what the rebuild makes.

OPERATIONS OWNED.
(1) B3, whole but the two things that answers-in-a-log puts into a log; B4, whole; of B5, its second half, how the rebuild comes to the answer that the tables hold. They are the rebuild and the comparison (implied spec 6.5 and 6.6).
(2) R1, as ruling 14 reads it, with the proof that ruling 14's last sentence asks. Of R7, the half that ruling 12 calls "of what a rebuild makes from the logs", and the second of ruling 12's two properties, shown by a run on a store where an attempt of each gate failed.
(3) Rulings 10, 13, 14 and 18; ruling 9 but the two choices that answers-in-a-log makes; of ruling 8, that the sets of strays are made from entries.
(4) As the last part, for the tree as the build leaves it: R2, R3, R5, R6, R8 and R11. Each part before it keeps each of these for what it changes. Of R9: rules 9 and 19 of BUILD-store-module.md (ruling 7).
(5) Of the implied spec: 5.2, edges 1 and 6 to 28, of which edge 18 is the second of the "Three things of the paper that are no open point" on the build's page; 4.9, its last paragraph; findings 9, 11 and 12, and finding 10 for a last stamp that is made again. Of the matrix: the block "x a rebuild" of each of 7.1 to 7.5, and 7.6. Where 7.1 says that the set of strays is made from the things on the depot, ruling 8 holds.
(6) Of section 9: of "From 'When this build passes'", item 4; "B4's list"; of "What the contract asks elsewhere", its lines 2 to 5; and "What a pass does not show", in the map of the rebuild's proof.
(7) Of the contract's "The builder chooses": its fourth line, with what that line says is not in this build.
(8) For the receipt: the list of every table with what it is made again from, and each thing that is not made again with its reason (B3; ruling 9).

WHAT TO FIGURE OUT.
1. The rebuild: what it is given (the logs, as ruling 18 says of them; the number of tasks, as ruling 9 says), what it may know of what it has made so far (ruling 10), and that it makes each part of each row of implied spec section 4 from the logs as the parts before left them, or names the part with its reason (B3; ruling 9).
2. What it makes, and where and for how long that is kept: the form is the plan's (the contract's "The builder chooses", its fourth line). R5 binds it, and finding 16, its first sentence, binds any table that it adds.
3. The comparison: what "equal" is (rulings 9 and 13), what the proof sends (B4, and the lines of section 9 named above), and how the proof hands the rebuild an answer that no gate of today would give (ruling 14).
4. What it does with what it cannot make: an entry with no act (edge 6), and an accepted act whose form the code of the day cannot give (ruling 14; edge 27).

THE TREE AS THIS PART LEAVES IT. The six proofs pass, and the rebuild's proof with them. The explanations are as the contract's "Explanations, as the tree's rules say" asks: the page for the rebuild with the four heads that it names, the row of the proofs' README, and the replacing of the line that nothing is built for a rebuild.

NOT THIS PART'S. A change to what a gate puts into a log: where a part of a row cannot be made from the logs as they are, that goes back to answers-in-a-log, whose state it is. The use of a rebuild on a running store (the contract's "The builder chooses", its fourth line; implied spec 5.2, edge 26). Nothing under the contract's "Not in this build, by decision".

hands_to_the_parts_after: It is the last part. To the review of the whole and to the receipt: the list of B3; each exception with its reason; and what the rebuild's proof does not show (section 9, its last paragraph; implied spec 5.2, edge 26).
